pairs.subject: lazy-section-addressability
pairs.evidence: src/components/MobilePageTOC.tsx:46 The mobile section list looks up the raw id once with getElementById. It never uses the shared resolver or a data-scroll-anchor wrapper, and it never waits for or re-lands on a lazy section, so on /features (LazyMount stages) a jump lands on the reserved stub and drifts as the sections above it mount.

techniques.evidence: src/components/MobilePageTOC.tsx:47 Scrolls once and smoothly, even for reduced-motion users. There is no bounded wait for the mounted section, no re-assertion after reserved height turns into real height, and focus does not move. It ignores the startArrival protocol that ScrollMap uses.

src/components/PageShell.tsx:34 Every PageShell page runs a dev-only check against the live DOM after first paint. It checks both directions, never throws, and its message names the address, the consumer and the page (src/hooks/useAnchorCoverageGuard.ts, src/lib/anchor-coverage.ts).

src/app/loading.tsx:13 This is the route-level loading boundary the technique names as a failure. In the newest build on disk (.next, 2026-10-16; loading.tsx unchanged since June), both /how.html and /index.html show the role=status Loading fallback, and the page sits inside `<div hidden id="S:0">` (event-bus wrapper at byte 50263, after the hidden div at 7081). So the address wrappers are in the bytes, but a reader without script cannot see or reach them.

pairs.subject: lazy-section-addressability
pairs.evidence: src/i18n/localeRelease.ts:2 These modules decide which locales ship and show a language offer. LocaleOffer reads only ?lang= from location.search and never touches the hash or scrolling. Searching src/i18n, src/components and src/stores for data-scroll-anchor, findAnchorGaps, ARRIVAL_BUDGET_MS and wrapperId found nothing, so these files neither host nor consume a lazy page's address space.

pairs.subject: lazy-section-addressability
pairs.evidence: src/app/how/page.tsx:86 The published hash sits on a styled StageSection, and the lazy section inside it later mounts with the same id. Address and internal handle are one string, and resolution depends on document order rather than on a declared wrapper/handle split.

techniques.evidence: src/app/how/page.tsx:86 The page renders the wrapper unconditionally, which is right. But the wrapper is the visual stage (glow, gradients, overflow-clip, scroll-mt), which the technique refuses: 'a wrapper that has acquired styling responsibilities'. There is also no data-scroll-anchor or focus target.

src/components/sections/how-manifesto/index.tsx:27 The inner section reuses the wrapper's published id (page.tsx:82), and the same is true for for-you, event-bus, agents-timeline, agents-chat and platform-layers. That leaves duplicate ids, one string serving both link and tracker, and no alias table.

src/app/how/page.tsx:60 Deep links rely on the browser's one-shot fragment scroll plus document order. Nothing re-lands after the ssr:false chunks mount, and nothing moves focus. The page's own jump consumers are the shared shell's: MobilePageTOC jumps once, and ScrollMap does nothing here (see notes).

src/components/sections/how-lazy.tsx:27 All four /how sections are client-only without a gate and without a recorded reason; the file header explains only the skeleton. These sections carry the page's explanatory meaning, which the tree says may not be client-only.

src/app/how/page.tsx:46 The vocabulary is declared by hand inline, and its hosts are plain ids. The shared guard's reverse direction (hosted without declaration) scans only [data-scroll-anchor], so on /how the check runs in one direction only. Declared-to-host does run, via InfoPageLayout/PageShell.

pairs.subject: lazy-section-addressability
pairs.evidence: src/lib/landing-address.ts:121 The arrival protocol is otherwise complete: it scrolls the wrapper, waits on a bounded retry, lands, moves focus, re-asserts, and cancels on reader intent. But exhaustion stops silently with no recorded event, and the location vocabulary is split across three hand-written lists.

techniques.evidence: src/app/page.tsx:67 The page renders an unstyled wrapper per manifest row, outside every condition. The section mounts inside a LazyMount stage with a minHeight reservation and mounts once.

src/lib/landing-address.ts:121 It has a 100ms/6000ms budget, re-resolves from the selector on each tick, re-asserts, cancels on intent, and supersedes older jumps. But useHashArrival.ts just stops on 'exhausted' and records nothing, which the technique refuses as 'exhaustion that leaves no trace'.

src/lib/landing-address.ts:50 There are two namespaces, with aliases kept forever (tools, download-section, use-cases). But the internal handles are a separate hand-written list beside LANDING_SECTIONS (constants.ts) and HOME_STAGES (home-manifest.ts), not one declaration. Source-scan tests catch drift between them.
src/lib/landing-address.test.ts:201 A CTA/link consumer guard backs up the live dev-time guard that runs through PageShell. home-manifest.test.ts pins the scroll map to the stages in both directions.

src/components/sections/lazy.tsx:44 The reason is recorded once per page, and home-manifest.test.ts fails if an ungated stage goes client-only. Gated placeholders carry the section label. The root loading.tsx hiding the visible document is judged under Layout.
